intended_object: The canonical ℤ-linear map ℚ ⊗_ℤ (ℝ/ℤ) → ℝ/ℚ sending q ⊗ [x] to the class of q·x modulo ℚ. It is induced by the bilinear map (q, [x]) ↦ q·[x] and is in fact the canonical isomorphism ℚ ⊗ ℝ/ℤ ≅ ℝ/ℚ. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the lemma rationalCircleDetector_tmul_coe.
explanation: The body is `TensorProduct.lift rationalCircleBilinear`. The bilinear map sends (q, m) to q • toRationalQuotient m. Here toRationalQuotient is the projection ℝ → ℝ ⧸ span_ℚ{1}, passed down through ℝ/ℤ (well defined because 1 lies in the rational span). The scalar action is the canonical ℚ-action on the quotient. The bilinearity side conditions use standard lemmas, and the tmul lemma confirms that q ⊗ [x] goes to [q x] mod ℚ, as the docstring says. ℝ ⧸ span_ℚ{1} is exactly ℝ/ℚ. This is a specific, canonical homomorphism (indeed the isomorphism ℚ⊗ℝ/ℤ ≅ ℝ/ℚ, since ℚ is flat over ℤ), so its specificity does not make it too narrow. It is correctly defined, and I found no Mathlib declaration for this particular map.
